name: P Nataraj
profile: Science graduate and Chartered Accountant, one of three brothers (with founder K.P. Ramasamy and K.P.D. Sigamani) behind KPR Mill, one of India's largest vertically integrated textile/apparel makers. As MD he oversees finance, cotton procurement and yarn marketing, and fronts the company's earnings calls.
interesting_fact: KPR began in 1984 as a small textile business, started exporting fashion apparel in 1989, and opened its first spinning unit at Sathyamangalam in 1995 with just 6,000 spindles.
deep_cut_fact: Despite being a CA, Nataraj's remit at KPR has long included the hands-on job of cotton procurement and yarn marketing, not just finance.
notes: Low public profile; route via company secretary/IR. Family also runs KPR Institute of Engineering and Technology trust.

name: Jesse Feldman
current_role: General Partner, Battery Ventures (Boston); leads its industrial-technology practice
profile: Boston-based private-equity/VC investor who joined Battery Ventures in 2005 and became a General Partner in 2012. He appears as a 10% owner of Sprinklr and Braze in SEC filings as one of the Battery Ventures fund reporting persons (shared fund holdings, not personal stakes). He focuses on buyout and growth-equity deals in industrial tech and life-science tools.
interesting_fact: Battery's industrial-technology practice he leads has completed 60+ transactions in the US and Europe since 2003; his exits include Drillinginfo, HighJump, Qognify and Rogue Wave Software, plus 40+ add-on acquisitions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Battery he was a founding member of Ionian Ventures, a fund focused on transportation and logistics technology, after starting his career at GE Capital; he holds a BA from Wesleyan and an MBA from Harvard.
notes: SEC 'net worth' figure reflects Battery Ventures fund holdings reported jointly by GPs, not his personal wealth. Relevant for industrial-tech/robotics angle (Robotiq, LI-COR boards).

name: Y Kasyap Reddy
current_role: Managing Director, Medha Group (Medha Servo Drives Pvt Ltd), Hyderabad
profile: Kasyap Reddy Yadavelli runs Medha, a privately held Hyderabad rail-technology group founded in 1984 that supplies propulsion electronics, traction motors and signalling systems to Indian Railways. Under him Medha has moved into full rolling stock (Vande Bharat propulsion, train sets) and opened a 100-acre coach factory near Hyderabad in 2023.
interesting_fact: Medha's Kondakal plant, inaugurated in June 2023, was billed as India's largest private rail coach factory, with planned capacity of 500 coaches and 50 locomotives a year; Medha also has a JV with Swiss maker Stadler Rail.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond rail, Medha has worked on solar inverters, battery-electric vehicle propulsion and canal automation, and signed an MoU to develop large propulsion motors for the Indian Navy.
notes: Private company, low-profile MD. marketing@ is the general sales/marketing address (no dedicated press address found). Relevant energy angle: electrification/propulsion, solar inverters.

profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China rich list (food industry, ~US$150m) via 'Xinrixian Group' (新日鲜). No web sources could be found in English or Chinese confirming the company or his current role.

name: Oleg Khaykin
current_role: President & CEO, VIAVI Solutions (NASDAQ: VIAV); director, Avnet
profile: Semiconductor and network-test executive who has led VIAVI since February 2016. Previously CEO of International Rectifier (2008 until its 2015 sale to Infineon) and a senior advisor at Silver Lake. VIAVI now pitches heavily into AI/data-center optical and high-speed Ethernet test (e.g. 1.6T validation, hollow-core fibre testing).
interesting_fact: He ran power-semiconductor maker International Rectifier from 2008 until Infineon acquired it in January 2015, then spent a year at Silver Lake before taking the VIAVI job.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an engineer at Motorola and spent eight years at Boston Consulting Group before moving into operating roles; he holds a B.S. with honors in electrical and computer engineering from Carnegie Mellon and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Strong data-center fit: VIAVI sells test gear for AI-fabric/optical interconnects. Best route is VIAVI PR (Grand Bridges).

name: Vrajmohan Shah
current_role: Founder, GSP Crop Science (Ahmedabad); no current directorships on MCA record
profile: Vrajmohan Ramanlal Shah founded GSP Crop Science in Ahmedabad in February 1985; it began in phosphate sales before moving into agrochemicals (crop-protection formulations and technicals). The company is now run by his son Bhavesh Shah (Chairman & MD) with the next generation (Executive Director Tirth Shah).
interesting_fact: GSP started out selling phosphates in 1985 before pivoting into agrochemicals around 1988, growing into one of India's larger privately held crop-protection makers.
notes: One aggregator profile refers to 'his demise', and the MCA register shows his DIN deactivated with zero current appointments, but no obituary was found, so alive status is unverified. If contacting, route via the company/Bhavesh or Tirth Shah (Tirth has given trade-press interviews, e.g. agribusinessglobal.com). Web-search budget ran out before contact research.

profile: Listed on Hurun India 2019 via Virchow Laboratories, a Hyderabad pharmaceutical/API maker incorporated in January 1982 at the Jeedimetla industrial estate (group also includes Virchow Biotech). name: Peter Dore Rawlinson
current_role: Former CEO & CTO, Lucid Group (step-down announced 25 Feb 2025); current role not confirmed
profile: Welsh-born automotive engineer (b. 1957) who held senior engineering roles at Jaguar and Lotus, was VP/chief vehicle engineer of the Tesla Model S (2009-2012), then joined Lucid as CTO in 2016 and became CEO in 2019, overseeing the Lucid Air and Gravity. He stepped down as CEO in 2025.
interesting_fact: A week after joining Tesla in 2009 he told Elon Musk the early Model S prototype was a 'false dawn' and restarted the car from a clean sheet; at Lucid he also oversaw the battery packs supplied to every Formula E team.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Bonvilston in the Vale of Glamorgan, attended Cowbridge Grammar School, and considered art school before choosing engineering at Imperial College (graduated 1979); in the 1980s his Jaguar team built the company's first intranet for moving engineering files.
notes: No longer Lucid CEO, so Lucid press office is not a good route; no personal site or verified social account found. Strong energy/battery angle (efficiency-focused EV powertrains).

name: Sohit Khurana
current_role: Co-owner/controller (with Manoj Jain) of Maso Capital Partners, Hong Kong; SEC reporting person for FiscalNote (NOTE)
profile: Hong Kong-based hedge-fund principal. SEC Form 4 filings (June 2025) state Maso Capital Partners, an Asia-focused event-driven/activist manager founded in 2013, is beneficially owned and controlled by Manoj Jain and Sohit Khurana. Maso sponsored the SPAC Duddell Street Acquisition, which merged with FiscalNote in 2022, hence the 10%+ stake (fund holdings).
interesting_fact: The FiscalNote shares are held via Duddell Street Holdings, named after Maso's office address at 6 Duddell Street in Central, Hong Kong.
notes: Very low profile: not listed on Maso's current leadership page (which shows Manoj Jain and Allan Finnerty), so his current day-to-day role is unclear. 'Net worth' reflects fund holdings he is deemed to control, not personal wealth.

name: Patrick Connor Haley
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner/CIO, Alta Fox Capital Management (Fort Worth, Texas)
profile: Connor Haley is the activist/value investor who launched the Alta Fox Opportunities Fund in 2018 after working at a New York long/short fund. Alta Fox is a 10%+ holder of LED-display maker Daktronics (DAKT), where it has been an engaged/activist shareholder; the SEC 'net worth' reflects fund holdings.
interesting_fact: He founded Alta Fox in Fort Worth rather than New York, and its flagship fund hunts 'overlooked and under-the-radar' opportunities across any asset class, market cap or geography.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Alta Fox he graduated magna cum laude from Harvard College with an A.B. in Government, not economics or finance.

public_contacts.value: Longacre Square Partners (media link on Alta Fox contact page points to gmarose@longacresquare.com)

notes: SEC name is Patrick Connor Haley; goes by Connor Haley. Active on X/fintwit historically but handle not verified here. Media inquiries routed via Longacre Square.

name: Barry F Cohen
current_role: COO - Americas and Board Member, SS Innovations International (SSII); Chairman, Avra Medical Robotics
profile: Veteran industrial-company manager and securities professional (50+ years) who founded Avra Surgical (2006) and Avra Medical Robotics (2015), the US shell that became SS Innovations International, maker of Dr. Sudhir Srivastava's low-cost SSi Mantra surgical robot. He now runs the company's Americas operations and sits on its board.
interesting_fact: His medical-robotics vehicle Avra became the US listing for SS Innovations, the Indian company behind the SSi Mantra surgical robotic system.
deep_cut_fact: Long before robotics he was a director of pipe and specialty-chemicals maker Synalloy Corp. (c.1979-1989) and its president in 1984-85, and ran his own NASD broker-dealer, Barry F. Cohen & Co., from 1983 to 1999.
notes: info@ is a general company address (no dedicated press/IR address found on the leadership page).

name: Chris Hulls
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Life360 (since Aug 2025; CEO Apr 2007-Aug 2025)
profile: Co-founded family-location app Life360 in April 2007 and ran it as CEO for 18 years, taking it public on the ASX and later Nasdaq and acquiring Tile and Jiobit; he moved to Executive Chairman in August 2025. He is also an angel investor/adviser to Tile, Ring, Automattic, Honk and Zendrive.
interesting_fact: When Life360 drew criticism from teenagers, Hulls opened a TikTok account to talk with them directly, which led to the 'Bubbles' feature that shares only an approximate location area.
deep_cut_fact: Before earning his business degree with highest honors at UC Berkeley, Hulls served in the United States Air Force.
notes: Publicly visible founder (TikTok, X). Best route is Life360 press office.

name: Alex Haro
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Hubble Network (since Oct 2021); Director, Life360
profile: Co-founded Life360 with Chris Hulls and served as its CTO (2008-2020) and President (2014-2020); he remains on Life360's board. Since 2021 he has been CEO of Hubble Network, which connects ordinary Bluetooth chips directly to satellites and a terrestrial gateway network for low-cost global IoT tracking.
interesting_fact: Hubble Network pitches 'space-grade' connectivity for any device with a standard Bluetooth chip - no modems or custom hardware - via its own satellites plus 100M+ phone gateways.
deep_cut_fact: Before Life360 he worked on Orbited, an open-source project for real-time browser networking; he studied computer science at Pomona College and was a Forbes 30 Under 30 (consumer tech) honoree in 2015.
notes: Great fit for an infrastructure/space-connectivity episode. Also co-founded MyMoneyKarma (India) in 2020. Best route: Hubble contact form or press page.

name: Snehal Patel
current_role: CEO, CFO and Director, Greenwich LifeSciences (NASDAQ: GLSI), Stamford CT
profile: Biotech executive and former healthcare investment banker (JP Morgan Chase, Sanders Morris Harris, Ferghana Partners) who runs Greenwich LifeSciences, a clinical-stage company developing GLSI-100 (GP2), a HER2 peptide immunotherapy aimed at preventing breast-cancer recurrence, now in the Phase III FLAMINGO-01 trial.
interesting_fact: He doubles as both CEO and CFO of the Nasdaq-listed company while it runs a global Phase III trial (FLAMINGO-01).
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer - BS in chemical engineering and MS in biochemical engineering from MIT - and early on worked in operations at Bayer and advised on disposable biotech manufacturing equipment and scale-up.
notes: Off-theme for energy/data centers; entrepreneurship angle only. No dedicated press/IR email published.
